'''Talithia D. Williams''' is an American [[Statistician]]. She also serves as a [[Mathematician|Mathematician Professor]] and Mathematics Clinic Director at [[Harvey Mudd College]], who researches the [[spatiotemporal]] structure of data.<ref name="AWM" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://gizmodo.com/these-black-female-mathematicians-should-be-stars-in-th-1792636094|title=These Black Female Mathematicians Should Be Stars in the Blockbusters of Tomorrow|last=Paoletta|first=Rae|work=Gizmodo|access-date=2017-04-08|language=en-US}}</ref>  Williams was the first African American Woman to achieve [[Academic tenure|tenure]] at [[Harvey Mudd College]].<ref name=":0" /> She is an advocate for engaging more African Americans in engineering and science fields.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/mariaklawe/2015/10/07/increasing-education-opportunities-for-minorities-in-stem/#1c7ffc79543f|title=Increasing Education Opportunities For Minorities In STEM|last=Klawe|first=Maria|work=Forbes|access-date=2017-04-08}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Talithia D. Williams was born in [[Columbus, Georgia]]. She attended [[Columbus High School (Columbus, Georgia)|Columbus High School]] where her appreciation for mathematical sciences was cultivated. She voluntarily competed in competitive math exams, where she was among the students who was advanced to the next round.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title={{!}} Talithia Williams |url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/talithia-williams/ |access-date=2025-03-05 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Williams is married to Donald Williams and they have three sons together.

==Education==
Williams attended [[Spelman College]] to obtain her bachelor's degree of science with a major in mathematics and a minor in physics.  Through the mentorship of the late  [[Claudia Alexander]], Williams participated in NASA’s [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] for three summer sessions while in undergrad. She then went on to obtain her graduate degree in mathematics at [[Howard University]]. Williams was a mentee in the 4-week residential [[EDGE Foundation|EDGE]] program, which is a mentorship organization that prepares people of color to gain their Ph.D. in the mathematics field.Then Williams attended [[Rice University]], where she gained a Ph.D. in Statistics.<ref name=":1" />

==Career and Research==
Williams has worked at the [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] (JPL), the [[National Security Agency]] (NSA), and [[NASA]].<ref name="AWM">{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/awm-elections-2015/talithia-williams-harvey-mudd-college|title=Talithia Williams, Harvey Mudd College - AWM Association for Women in Mathematics|website=sites.google.com|access-date=2017-04-08}}</ref><ref name="TED">{{Cite news|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/talithia_williams|title=Talithia Williams {{!}} Speaker {{!}} TED.com|last=Williams|first=Talithia|access-date=2017-04-08|language=en}}</ref> She is an associate professor of mathematics and also serves as Associate Dean for Research and Experiential Learning at [[Harvey Mudd College]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematics Faculty |url=https://www.hmc.edu/mathematics/people/faculty/ |website=Harvey Mudd Department of Mathematics |accessdate=20 August 2018}}</ref><ref name = "AWM" /><ref name = "TED" /> She is Secretary and Treasurer for the [[EDGE Foundation]] which sponsors summer programs for minority women, and on the boards of the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]] and [[Society for the Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science|SACNAS]].<ref name="AWM" />  Williams has done significant outreach, with the goal of bringing mathematics to life and "rebranding the field of mathematics as anything but dry, technical or male-dominated but instead a logical, productive career path that is crucial to the future of the country."<ref name="HMC">{{Cite web |title=Talithia Williams : Harvey Mudd College |url=https://www.math.hmc.edu/~twilliams/ |access-date=2017-04-08 |website=www.math.hmc.edu}}</ref><ref name="APB">{{Cite web|url=http://www.apbspeakers.com/speaker/talithia-williams|title=Talithia Williams {{!}} Book for Speaking, Events and Appearances|date=2015-12-16|website=www.apbspeakers.com|language=en|access-date=2017-04-08}}</ref>

Williams has developed statistical models focused on understanding the structure of spatiotemporal data, with environmental applications.<ref name="AWM" /><ref name="MackGazette">{{Cite web|url=http://www.gvsu.edu/mackinacgazette/mosaic-talithia-williams-29.htm|title=Mosaic: Talithia Williams - Mackinac Gazette - Grand Valley State University|website=www.gvsu.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-04-08}}</ref> She has partnered with the [[World Health Organization]] in developing a cataract model used to predict the cataract surgical rate for countries in Africa.<ref name="MackGazette" />

Williams was a host of two [[PBS]] series; (1) Six-part NOVA Wonders in April 2018, and (2) five-part NOVA Universe Revealed in November 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=Meet Talithia Williams |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/video/meet-talithia-williams/ |website=NOVA Wonders |access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref> She is the author of the book ''[[Power in Numbers: The Rebel Women of Mathematics]]'' (Race Point Publishing, 2018).<ref>Reviews of ''Power in Numbers: The Rebel Women of Mathematics'':

*{{cite journal|last=Lawrence|first=Emille Davie|date=February 2019|issue=2|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|pages=251–253|title=Review|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201902/rnoti-p251.pdf|volume=66|doi=10.1090/noti1800|doi-access=free}}
*{{cite journal|last1=Cabrera Arnau|first1=Carmen|last2=Kalaydzhieva|first2=Nikoleta|date=March 2019|journal=Chalkdust|title=Review|url=https://chalkdustmagazine.com/blog/book-review-power-in-numbers/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Williams' Book Highlights Female Mathematicians|work=Harvey Mudd College News|date=June 11, 2018|url=https://www.hmc.edu/about-hmc/2018/06/11/williams-book-highlights-female-mathematicians/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=NOVA Universe Revealed|url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/series/nova-universe-revealed|website=NOVA|date=27 October 2021 |accessdate=25 November 2021}}</ref>

=== TED Talk ===
In 2014, Williams gave a highly viewed [[TED (conference)|TED talk]] titled "Own Your Body's Data".<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_GMVTJ9ZKVc "Own Your Body's Data"]</ref> In this speech, she expressed the importance of collecting data and how data can help you make well-informed decisions. She goes on to mention her third pregnancy experience, where the doctor's advised her to be induced at 41 and 1/2 weeks due to the baby being under stress. After initial concern of the inconsistency of the stress testing,  Williams seeks additional data by asking questions. Once the additional data is obtained, her husband and herself decided against being induced because the data did not prove a necessity for an induction.  She then provided other personal examples to express the importance of knowing all the data in order to make well-informed decisions.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_GMVTJ9ZKVc |title=Talithia Williams: Own your body's data |date=2014-08-11 |last=TED |access-date=2025-03-05 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Williams challenged the audience to utilize data to take charge of their own health.

==Awards/Honors==
In 2015, Williams received the [[Mathematical Association of America|MAA]] Henry L. Alder Award for exemplary teaching by an early career mathematics professor.<ref>{{cite web|title=Henry L. Adler Award|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/teaching-awards/henry-l-alder-award|website=Mathematical Association of America|accessdate=10 April 2017}}</ref> Williams was honored by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] and the Mathematical Association of America, when they selected her to be the [[AWM/MAA Falconer Lecturer]] at MathFest 2017 in Chicago, IL.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/node/832050/|title=Invited Lectures at MathFest 2017|website=Mathematical Association of America|access-date=10 April 2017}}</ref> The title of her talk is "Not So Hidden Figures: Unveiling Mathematical Talent." Williams was also recognized by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2017 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Talithia Williams|url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/talithia-williams/|access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref> She received the 2022 [[Joint Policy Board for Mathematics]] Communication Award "for bringing mathematics and statistics into the homes of millions through her work as a TV host, renowned speaker, and author."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Statistician Talithia Williams is the 2022 JPBM Communications Award Recipient|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/statistician-talithia-williams-is-the-2022-jpbm-communications-award-recipient-1|access-date=2021-09-13|website=SIAM News|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Meetings (JMM) |first=Joint Mathematics |title=Joint Mathematics Meetings |url=https://www.jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2022/2268_prizes-all |access-date=2022-06-19 |website=Joint Mathematics Meetings |language=en}}</ref>
